info.title: Print.App API
info.description: Server-to-server API for Print.App integrations: designs and their page content, folders, files, fonts, palettes, product assignments, projects and editor links. Authenticate every request with a secret key: `Authorization: Bearer sk_…`. Never call it from a browser.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The account a secret key belongs to.

tags.name: Designs
tags.description: The designs (templates) your customers start from: create them at a size, manage their pages, and place text, images and shapes on them.

tags.name: Design folders
tags.description: Folders that organise your designs. A design can sit in more than one folder.

tags.name: Files
tags.description: Your own images and graphics, used in designs and offered to customers in the editor.

tags.name: Graphic folders
tags.description: Folders of files, shown in the editor under Pictures, Backgrounds, Textures or Frames.

tags.name: Fonts
tags.description: The fonts your designs and customers can use: the built-in set, imported Google fonts and fonts you upload.

tags.name: Palettes
tags.description: Colour palettes offered in the editor.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Which designs open for each product (and variant) in your store.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: Your customers' saved designs.

tags.name: Links
tags.description: Project URLs (the dashboard's Create new Project URL): shareable links that open a design or project in the editor at create.print.app, to share with customers or to test a design.

tags.name: Connectors
tags.description: Links between the options on a store's product page and the editor: the choice a customer makes shows the right pages, opens the right design, or sets the size, orientation or colour. Read a product page for what a connector can point at, and test one against a design before customers meet it.

tags.name: Print Options
tags.description: Print Options is Print.App's free product options app (options.print.app): the sizes, papers, quantities and prices customers choose on a product page, priced on our servers when they add to cart. An option set is those questions and their prices; Print.App designs fill its artwork step, and connectors read its answers. Option sets are managed here for Shopify stores with both apps installed; templates and quotes work for any account.

tags.name: Resource profiles
tags.description: Limits on the fonts, colour palettes and graphic folders the editor offers, for the designs that use them.

tags.name: PDF profiles
tags.description: The settings print PDFs are made with: colour conversion, PDF standard, cut lines, image resolution, fonts.

tags.name: 3D scenes
tags.description: The 3D scenes the editor previews designs on: models with print areas, folds, flipbooks and sheets, yours and the Print.App library's. A design picks one with `sceneId`.

tags.name: Library
tags.description: The Print.App library, the store catalogue the dashboard's Import Designs and Import from Library open: ready-made designs, and themed kits of graphics. Find what suits a product, then bring it into your account: a design as your own copy, a kit as a folder that follows it, single graphics into a folder.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: The account's editor and product page settings: how the editor opens and behaves, and the selectors Print.App uses on your product pages. Settings that run code in your store, send data elsewhere or delete projects are kept to the dashboard.

post.description:
Adds, changes and removes text, images, shapes, frames, QR codes and other items on a design's pages, as one batch of operations. The batch is checked against the operation schemas first and refused as a whole if any operation is malformed (400). It then runs in order; if any operation fails, nothing is saved (422). With `dryRun: true` it runs without saving.

Place images and SVG graphics as files: upload them with `POST /v2/files` (from a URL) or `POST /v2/files/uploads`, then give the file id as `asset`. An SVG file stays vector in print. Don't send SVG markup inline (`svg`): the firewall in front of the API refuses request bodies that carry markup, with an HTML 403.

- `pageIndex`: Shows only the pages a choice maps to (`to`: page numbers such as `1` or `1,2`). The other pages are set aside: not shown, printed or saved.
- `designSelector`: Opens another design for each choice (`to`: a design id). Every design it can open must be assigned to the product and carry this connector too.
- `pageClone`: Repeats one page (`page`, default the first) as many times as the number chosen, when the editor opens.
- `pageCount`: Sends the number of pages to the field as the customer adds or removes pages (editor to product page).
- `printedPageCount`: Sends the number of pages (sides) that carry a print to the field, so the price can follow (editor to product page). The field takes a number.
- `pageWidth`: Sets the page width from a number field, in the design's unit (a Print Options size field carries its own). With twoWay, a resize in the editor is sent back.
- `pageHeight`: Sets the page height from a number field, in the design's unit (a Print Options size field carries its own). With twoWay, a resize in the editor is sent back.
- `pageOrientation`: Turns the pages (or `page` alone) landscape or portrait, from the choice's wording or its mapping (`to`: landscape or portrait).
- `textValue`: Puts what the customer types into the text item titled `text`. With twoWay, edits in the editor are sent back.
- `underlayColor`: Sets the product colour of an underlay design (a T-shirt, a mug): `to` is a hex colour, or leave the choice unmapped when it is the colour's name in the design.
- `event`: Fires an editor event (`event.name`, with `event.data`) when the field changes. For integrations that listen to editor events.

Error.title: Error
Error.description: Every error the API itself returns. Match on `code`; `message` is for people and may be reworded.

code.description: `unauthorized` (401): missing, unknown, revoked or expired secret key. `account_suspended` (403): the account has an unpaid invoice. `invalid_request` (400): a parameter or body field is malformed — see `param` and `details`. `not_found` (404): no such resource in your account. `route_not_found` (404): no such endpoint. `idempotency_key_reused` (409): the Idempotency-Key was used for a different request. `idempotency_in_progress` (409): the first request with that key is still running. `folder_not_empty` (409): the folder still holds designs or folders. `builtin_folder`, `builtin_palette` (409): Print.App's own folders and palettes cannot be changed. `editor_not_supported` (409): page content can only be edited on accounts that use the new editor. `design_changed` (409): the design was saved elsewhere while the batch ran; read it again and retry. `payload_too_large` (413): a body or file over the limit. `unsupported_media_type` (415): send JSON. `ops_failed` (422): an operation in the batch failed, nothing was saved — see `details`. `internal_error` (500): retry; contact support with the `requestId` if it persists. `service_unavailable` (503): retry in a few seconds.

param.description: The parameter or body field at fault, as a path (`pages[0].title`).

details.description: Every problem found, when there was more than one (`invalid_request`), or each operation's result (`ops_failed`).

requestId.description: Also sent as the `x-request-id` header. Quote it when contacting support.

examples.message: limit must be an integer from 1 to 100.

DesignOpItemUpdate.description: Changes an item. Items added earlier in the same batch take any property of the op that added them. Items already on the saved design take: box, content, font, size, weight, style, color, leading, tracking, align, anchor, fill, stroke, opacity, rotate, lock, field, asset, svg, cornerRadius.
